Interface RouteMatchSelector

public interface RouteMatchSelector
Selects among the routes that match a request, instead of the Micronaut route selection policy, and negotiates the media type of the response. A route gets a selector with RouteSpec#selectedBy(RouteMatchSelector), or from its groups; the routes of a template language usually share one selector, e.g. one per JAX-RS application.

The router calls it when every route that matches the path of a request, and accepts its method, port, conditions, content type (RouteInfo.doesConsume(MediaType)) and accepted types (RouteInfo.doesProduce(Collection)), has the same selector, the same instance, even when there is only one such route, instead of the Micronaut resolution of ambiguous routes by the media types and the specificity of the templates. For the routes of a selector the types are compatible when one matches the other, without the parameters: Accept: image/* reaches the routes that produce image/png and image/*; when none is compatible the router answers 406 or 415 as for other routes. When the candidates have different selectors, or none, the Micronaut policy selects, and no selector is called. For example a JAX-RS selector selects by the specificity of JAX-RS (section 3.7.2), then by the content type of the request against @Consumes and the accepted types, with their quality, against @Produces, with their qs.

A locator route is never given to select(HttpRequest, List): its target is located after the selection. When locator routes are among the candidates and they all have the same selector, the router keeps the most specific of them by the order of the selector, or by the Micronaut policy. The selection is therefore not staged as in JAX-RS: a resource method that the media types exclude does not keep a request from a locator route of the same path.

When the router finds the routes of the path of every HTTP method (Router.findAny(HttpRequest)), e.g. for the 405 status and its Allow header, or a CORS preflight request, it calls the selector for the matches of each method, given as above for a request of that method, and a route of the selector counts only when it is selected. A route the selector does not select for the method of the request is not found, and a method none of whose routes is selected is not allowed.

The matches are normal route matches: filters, argument binding and the annotations of the route apply to the selected match as to any other. The negotiated media type of a selection reaches the handler as UriRouteMatch.getSelectedMediaType() and selectedMediaType(io.micronaut.http.PathVariables), and is the content type of the response when the handler does not set one.

  • Method Details

    • select

      List<RouteMatchSelector.Selection> select(HttpRequest<?> request, List<UriRouteMatch<?,?>> matches)
      Select among the matches of a request.
      Parameters:
      request - The request
      matches - The matches of the path, of the routes of this selector, in the order of the route table: at least one
      Returns:
      The selected matches, each one of the given matches: one to route the request, none for no route (404, or the status the router answers for a path no route matches), and more than one when the selector does not decide: the router then prefers, as for other routes, a route of the method of the request over a route of any method, an explicit route over an implicit HEAD route, and the lowest order, and the request is ambiguous if they are equal

    • order

      default Optional<Comparator<UriRouteInfo<?,?>>> order()
      The order of specificity of the routes of this selector, where select(HttpRequest, List) cannot run: when locator routes are among the candidates, see the class documentation. The template a locator route was declared with is locatorPrefix(UriRouteInfo). compare(a, b) < 0 means a is more specific than b; routes that compare equal are equally specific, and a request both match is ambiguous.
      Returns:
      The order, or empty for the Micronaut policy
